about: Units duel: the unit of the result is given; exactly one of four expressions can be right by dimensions alone. Trains the dimension check as a reflex. 75 seconds per question. SI units throughout. After each answer the units of every symbol in the question are listed (symbols table). Each question has a 'meaning' hint (what the quantity is, without units) with the script section.

items.q: Energy of a quantum of the oscillator
items.why: $[\hbar]=\mathrm{J\,s}$, $[\omega]=\mathrm{s^{-1}}$: only $\hbar\omega$ is an energy.
items.meaning: The energy step between neighbouring levels of the harmonic oscillator: what one excitation (one quantum of that frequency) carries.

items.why: $[h]=\mathrm{J\,s}=\mathrm{kg\,m^2/s}$, $[p]=\mathrm{kg\,m/s}$: $h/p$ is a length. $h/(mc^2)$ is a time.
items.meaning: The wavelength of the wave that belongs to a particle of given momentum: the larger the momentum, the shorter the wave.

items.why: $\sqrt{2mE}$ is a momentum, and momentum over $\hbar$ is a wave number. Without the root you get momentum squared over $\hbar$.
items.meaning: Inside a barrier higher than the energy, the wave function does not oscillate but decays; $\kappa$ says how fast, and $1/\kappa$ is how deep the particle reaches into the barrier.

items.why: $e^2/4\pi\epsilon_0$ is energy times length. $\hbar^2/m$ is energy times length squared. Their ratio is a length. The last option is a velocity ($\alpha c$).
items.meaning: The radius of the lowest orbit in Bohr’s hydrogen model: the natural size of atoms, where the Coulomb attraction balances the cost of confining the electron.

items.q: Ground-state energy of a box of width $a$
items.why: $\hbar k$ is a momentum with $k\sim1/a$, and $p^2/2m$ is an energy: $\hbar^2/(ma^2)$.
items.meaning: The lowest energy of a particle trapped between two infinitely high walls. It is never zero: confinement forces a minimum momentum.

items.q: Oscillator length (width of the ground state)
items.why: $\hbar/(m\omega)$ has units $\mathrm{m^2}$, so the root is a length. $\sqrt{\hbar\omega/m}$ is a velocity.
items.meaning: How far the Gaussian ground state of the oscillator spreads out; every oscillator wave function is measured in this length.

items.q: Transition rate (golden rule), $\rho(E)$ = states per energy
items.why: $|V|^2\rho$ is energy$^2$ per energy = energy; energy over $\hbar$ is a rate.
items.meaning: How quickly a weak perturbation drives a system from its initial state into a continuum of final states (Fermi’s golden rule).

items.why: A magnetic moment is charge over mass times angular momentum: $\frac{e}{m}\hbar$. The version with $1/c$ is the Gaussian form and is off by a velocity in SI.
items.meaning: The natural size of an electron’s magnetic moment: the moment of an electron carrying one quantum of angular momentum.

items.q: Fermi energy of a free-electron gas of density $n$
items.why: $k_F=(3\pi^2n)^{1/3}$ is a wave number ($n$ is per volume), and $\hbar^2k^2/2m$ is an energy: the power must be $2/3$.
items.meaning: The energy of the highest occupied electron state at zero temperature, when all electrons fill the lowest states two by two (Pauli).

items.why: $j=nev$ and $v=\frac{e\tau}{m}E$: $\sigma=ne\cdot\frac{e\tau}{m}$. With one $e$ you have $n$ times the mobility divided by a charge.
items.meaning: How much current flows per applied field when electrons are accelerated by the field and lose their momentum in collisions every $\tau$ on average.

items.why: $ne$ is a charge density, $\mathrm{C/m^3}$; its inverse is volume per charge.
items.meaning: The transverse (Hall) field per current density and magnetic field. Its sign tells the sign of the carriers, its size their density.

items.why: $k_D=(6\pi^2n)^{1/3}$ is a wave number, $v_sk_D$ a frequency, $\hbar\omega_D$ an energy, and energy over $k_B$ a temperature.
items.meaning: The temperature that belongs to the highest phonon frequency of the Debye model: far above it every mode is excited (Dulong–Petit), far below it the heat capacity grows like $T^3$.

items.q: Sound velocity of the monatomic chain (spring $C$, mass $M$, spacing $a$)
items.why: $[C]=\mathrm{N/m}=\mathrm{kg/s^2}$, so $\sqrt{C/M}$ is a frequency; times a length gives a velocity.
items.meaning: The slope of the acoustic branch $\omega(k)$ at small $k$: how fast long-wavelength vibrations (sound) run along a chain of masses joined by springs.

items.q: Electronic heat capacity per volume of a metal
items.why: $nk_B$ already has the units of a heat capacity per volume; $T/T_F$ is a pure number (the fraction of electrons that can be excited).
items.meaning: The heat that warms the conduction electrons per volume and per degree. Only electrons within about $k_BT$ of the Fermi energy can take up energy.

items.why: Force $evB$ = $m^*v\omega$: $\omega=eB/m^*$. Check: $[eB]=\mathrm{C\,T}=\mathrm{kg/s}$.
items.meaning: The angular frequency at which a carrier circles in a magnetic field; resonant absorption at this frequency measures the effective mass.

items.q: Width of the depletion layer of a p–n junction
items.why: Poisson: $V\sim\frac{eN}{\epsilon\epsilon_0}w^2$, so $w^2\sim\frac{\epsilon\epsilon_0V}{eN}$: the expression without the root is an area, the last one an inverse length.
items.meaning: The thickness of the region around a p–n interface that is emptied of free carriers; the fixed ionised dopants left there carry the built-in voltage.

items.why: $GM/r$ is a velocity squared (escape speed), so $GM/c^2$ is a length.
items.meaning: The radius at which the escape speed from a mass equals the speed of light: the horizon of a non-rotating black hole.

items.q: Free-fall (dynamical) time of a cloud of density $\rho$
items.why: $[G\rho]=\mathrm{s^{-2}}$ (from $\ddot r\sim GM/r^2\sim G\rho r$): the inverse root is a time.
items.meaning: How long a cloud without pressure needs to collapse under its own gravity; it depends only on its density.

items.why: Balance $\frac{L\sigma_T}{4\pi r^2c}=\frac{GMm_p}{r^2}$: $L=\frac{4\pi GMm_pc}{\sigma_T}$. $GMm_p$ is energy times length; times $c$ over an area is a power.
items.meaning: The luminosity at which the push of radiation on electrons (Thomson scattering) balances gravity on the protons; brighter objects blow away their outer layers.

items.why: Sound speed times the free-fall time $1/\sqrt{G\rho}$: a length.
items.meaning: The smallest size of a region that collapses under its own gravity despite its pressure: larger perturbations grow, smaller ones just oscillate as sound waves.

items.why: $aT^4$ is an energy density, and pressure has the units of energy density. $\sigma T^4$ is a flux ($\mathrm{W/m^2}$): it differs by a velocity.
items.meaning: The pressure exerted by blackbody radiation (a photon gas in thermal equilibrium); it matters in the most massive stars.

items.why: $H_0$ is a velocity per distance, $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$. $c/H_0$ is the Hubble length.
items.meaning: Roughly the age of the universe if it had always expanded at today’s rate: the time galaxies needed to reach their present separations.

items.why: $[G\rho]=\mathrm{s^{-2}}$ again: $\rho\sim H_0^2/G$.
items.meaning: The density at which the universe is spatially flat: the dividing line between expanding forever and recollapsing (without a cosmological constant).

items.q: Virial temperature of a gas cloud (mass $M$, radius $R$)
items.why: $k_BT\sim$ gravitational energy per particle, $GMm_p/R$.
items.meaning: The temperature a self-gravitating gas cloud must have so that the thermal energy of its particles balances its gravitational binding (virial theorem).

items.q: Mass scale of the Chandrasekhar limit
items.why: $\hbar c/G$ is a mass squared (the Planck mass squared). To the power $3/2$ it is a mass cubed; divided by $m_p^2$ a mass.
items.meaning: The largest mass a star held up by degenerate electron pressure can have; above it, relativistic degenerate electrons can no longer resist gravity.
